video_title: Jim Jackson Talks Toni Braxton Incident, Jason Kidd, Kobe Bryant, Yao Ming, Rookie Holdout & More!

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Shaquille O'Neal's eligibility for summer camps
quotes.excerpt: Shaq could not play or go to camps out of state or he'll be ineligible.
quotes.quote: Kenny Anderson was the number one player. Keep in mind, Shaq was in our class. But Shaq at that time, because Texas had these rules where Shaq could not play or go to camps out of state or he'll be ineligible. So while we were going to Nike and Five-Star, Shaq couldn't go. So we heard of Shaq, but we couldn't see him until post-high school. We played in the Dapper Dan game in Pittsburgh.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Kenny Anderson's high school impact
quotes.excerpt: How big Kenny Anderson was is kind of like how big LeBron was in high school.
quotes.quote: In the lineage of point guards, you think about Rod Strickland, Kenny Smith, Mark Jackson, guys of that all out of New York. But you think about it, I tell people this, how big Kenny Anderson was is kind of like how big LeBron James was in high school without the social media. Absolutely. But what added to the nostalgia was that you didn't see him because you didn't have social media. So it made it a little bit more impactful and special when you were able to see Kenny play.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on his recruitment to Georgia Tech
quotes.excerpt: Kenny called me and said, 'Yo Jim, I'm going to Georgia Tech.'
quotes.quote: Kenny called me and said, 'Yo Jim, I'm going to Georgia Tech.' I was like, 'What?' Georgia Tech was never, because it was again, North Carolina for us and also Georgetown. Never was Georgia Tech discussed. Out of nowhere, Bobby Cremins did his thing, got him down from New York.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Abdul-Rauf's offensive ability
quotes.excerpt: Kenny Anderson said that was the one guy that gave him the most problems.
quotes.quote: Kenny Anderson said that was the one guy that gave him the most problems. Keep in mind, Kenny wasn't known to be the best defensive player. His offense was his best defense. But at that time, Chris was probably, out of Mississippi, one of the top point guards in the country, of course. But what people forget is how athletic Chris was. 42-inch vertical, I know this. He lost a little bit of it when he went to LSU when he gained that weight after his freshman year.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Tim Hardaway's development at UTEP
quotes.excerpt: Tim was relatively unknown going to UTEP. And he started to develop his name and his game.
quotes.quote: Tim was relatively unknown going to UTEP. And he started to develop his name and his game while he was there. And he had the crossover, but Chris's crossover was through the leg pull-up, more so than the crossover. His counter though was through the leg cross, jumper. For sure.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on his recruitment to Ohio State
quotes.excerpt: They were waiting for that matchup with he and Kenny Anderson, but Kenny had to go to summer school.
quotes.quote: They were waiting for that matchup with he and Kenny Anderson, but Kenny had to go to summer school that year.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Gary Williams' influence at Ohio State
quotes.excerpt: Gary Williams before he left, he recruited me. He started getting a Perry Carter out of DC.
quotes.quote: Gary Williams before he left, he recruited me. He started getting a Perry Carter out of DC, McDonald's All-American, the Treg Lee out of Cleveland, a Mark Baker, Chris Jent. He started getting these guys committed to Ohio State. So he laid the foundation and I said, 'Well, I could be a foundational piece and we can do something pretty special.' And that's what ended ultimately happened.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the impact of being drafted
quotes.excerpt: Just because you're talented, doesn't ultimately lead to the success that that talent warrants.
quotes.quote: It's a prime indication where just because you're talented, doesn't ultimately lead to the success that that talent warrants. And it depends a lot of times on system. My understanding, and again, let's go back to the draft. Harold was projected in the top six. I remember back in the day, I don't know if you remember this, Nike ventured out and tried to be agents. So Harold, I believe signed with Nike. So they guaranteed, I think, I think that he would be in the top six. He ended up going 13th. So think about that shift. Six at the time, the Alonzo Mourning went to Denver, might have been Spoon at six that went to Philly. So maybe if that's Harold going to Philly, he doesn't have to deal with Coach Loughery in Miami who didn't really like him, who didn't like rookies from my understanding. Coupled with the fact that you had Bimbo Coles, Brian Shaw, Steve Smith at guards already. So it wasn't like Harold had the chance, like some of the other guys on our class, to go right in and play and establish himself.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the rookie draft scale
quotes.excerpt: First pick got six years, 33. And then it just trickled down.
quotes.quote: First pick got six years, 33. And then it just trickled down. Second pick Alonzo Mourning, Christian Laettner signed. So it was my time to sign. But the Mavericks didn't get that memo because they were stuck on, well, their two previous years of draft picks didn't quite pan out. So they didn't feel that paying a guard a six-year 20-some million dollar deal made sense. So what they were offering was what maybe the eighth pick was going to get. And we're like, 'Hold up.' One thing we're not going to do, I'm not taking less than what the fifth pick got, but I'm not asking for more than what the third pick. So there's a market in between there. Perfect sense.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on his rookie holdout
quotes.excerpt: I got tested that year because I remember Donald Carter, rest in peace, he was the owner.
quotes.quote: I got tested that year because I remember Donald Carter, rest in peace, he was the owner for the Mavericks at the time. I was living in Columbus. This is a lengthy holdout already, the season had already started. And I preface this by saying that people say they're going to hold out, you hear it all the time, baseball, football, basketball, hockey, until it's really time when you're not getting paid. Then where's your resolve and what you really believe in? Is it about the money? Yeah, but is it about the principle, too? Those things tend to collide a little bit when one is not met. And most of the time it's the money. I was a rookie. I didn't, I mean, I had a Nike deal, I had a that time a trading card deal, so I was cool. So Donald Carter flies to Columbus, we meet, he explains his side of the story as to why he doesn't want to pay me. And said we're willing to offer you a million dollar signing bonus right now. And I said, 'Mr. Carter, no disrespect, I never had a million dollars. I don't know what I'm missing, but I'm not going to sign for what the market says I should less than what the market said I should get.' So if you don't want to pay me, you can trade the pick, or I'm going back to school. So it was it was really contentious at the time.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on adjusting his game after injury
quotes.excerpt: I had to adjust my game because I wasn't as athletic as I was before.
quotes.quote: I had to adjust my game because I wasn't as athletic as I was before. So I had to play multiple ways. I had to be more grounded. My passing got, well I was always a good passer, but my shooting got better, defensively got better, rebounding, because I had to do all the other things to basically make up for not having the athleticism.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the mental aspect of being traded
quotes.excerpt: It's still a mental part of a player, I believe, when you get traded, that's like, okay, this team didn't want me.
quotes.quote: It's still a mental part of a player, I believe, when you get traded, that's like, okay, this team didn't want me. It's still a little bit a part of that. But at the end of the day, you still got to be a pro. Because no matter whether you agree with it or not, the team traded you, you still got a job to do. So you going to sulk and be upset over here, and then it's going to impact you over here because you're not playing well because you're mad about the trade over here. That's the part after that first trade that you learn. You still got to be a pro.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on refusing to play for New Orleans
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going. Real talk. It was after Christmas, had a good game.
quotes.quote: I'm not going. Real talk. It was after Christmas, had a good game. Jeff Van Gundy and I, who I work with now at the Clippers, man he used to come talk to me all the time about the team and I was one of the captains. So I was very secure in Houston. I got, you know, Christmas Day, Jeff calls me, I'm thinking he calling me, you know, like we usually talk, and he said, Jimmy, we made a trade. I'm like, okay, we made a trade, because we know we talk. And he said, we traded Bo Outlaw and you to New Orleans for, it was David Wesley, somebody else. I said, excuse me? I can remember sitting in, I had a little office in my house at the time in Houston, and he told me to trade again. I was like, oh really? I said, that's interesting. I said, that's cold, but I'm not going.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Byron Scott as a coach
quotes.excerpt: Byron Scott was the coach at the time.
quotes.quote: Byron Scott was the coach at the time. I said, I've been on multiple teams. I've been through a different path than you have. So my perspective is different than you. Of course, you wouldn't do it, but what I've been through tells me this is not what I want to do. I don't want to go through the point of coming down there and being unhappy and then being traded later over the summer. So I'm not, I don't want to come.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Chris Paul joining New Orleans
quotes.excerpt: Chris Paul there too, right?
quotes.quote: Chris Paul there too, right? This was 2004, 2005. I said, I appreciate it, but I'm not, I'm not coming. And they were like, well, we going to find you for when you don't come. I said, well, you just got to have to find me. I'm not, I stuck it out in Houston, end up getting to Phoenix.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the league's rule change regarding trades
quotes.excerpt: They instituted a rule where you would get fined not only by the team but by the league.
quotes.quote: They instituted a rule where you would get fined not only by the team but by the league if you didn't report to the team you got traded to. So think about that, I had a holdout my rookie year. There you go. That's what I was going to mention that. And it comes back to this, this damn Jimmy Jackson. We we go again, bucking the system. But at that time, I wanted to have control over my career. For so long, outside of free agency, I didn't. At that point, I just said, I'm tired mentally. I'm not going down to New Orleans. I'm just, I'm just not.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on no-trade clauses
quotes.excerpt: You got to have leverage to do that. They're not giving it to a eighth, ninth man.
quotes.quote: You got to have leverage to do that. They're not giving it to a eighth, ninth man, tenth man they're trying to sign. I was just curious. Oh, you did. That's right. But it was, that was an act of, you could do that back then. If you were, I mean, you were Jimmy Jackson. You averaged 25, 26 points. That was 94. This was 2005. Far removed from that. No leverage. No leverage. So I couldn't negotiate something like that.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on his time with the Phoenix Suns
quotes.excerpt: It was special. And that's when it was seven seconds or less.
quotes.quote: It was special. And that's when it was seven seconds or less. So coming from Houston shooting three, I, I mean, I fit. It was to the point where if you open and you don't shoot it, we not passing it back to you. But it wasn't a forced situation. It was because the ball moves so much that you're going to get open shot. And it was going from being in Houston to kind of underachieving with Yao and Tracy because of the expectations, to playing in that free flowing offense in Phoenix was just, bro, it was money.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Yao Ming and Tracy McGrady
quotes.excerpt: Because of the expectations, to playing in that free flowing offense in Phoenix was just, bro, it was money.
quotes.quote: Because of the expectations, to playing in that free flowing offense in Phoenix was just, bro, it was money. Going from being in Houston to kind of underachieving with Yao and Tracy because of the expectations, to playing in that free flowing offense in Phoenix was just, bro, it was money.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Yao Ming's intelligence
quotes.excerpt: Yao knew exactly what he was doing.
quotes.quote: Yao knew exactly what he was doing. I'm not going to say it was the best, but he knew. But he knew. He understood. Oh, yeah, big time. Okay. Yeah, no, Yao was very intelligent. Knew how to play the media part of it of when he needed to speak or when he didn't. I love playing with Yao. Yao was one of the best, man. Unbelievable.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Tracy McGrady's talent
quotes.excerpt: One of the most talented players I've ever seen in my life.
quotes.quote: One of the most talented players I've ever seen in my life. I mean, just physically gifted, right hand, left hand, what he could do on the court. Right. Um, it was, because you hear a lot and you saw him playing on Orlando, but then you get a chance to see him move and he was just different, long, athletic. I think injuries plagued the back end of his career on how great he could have really been. I don't know if he had the same mentality that a Kobe Bryant, that all out just was this was it.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Kobe Bryant's mentality
quotes.excerpt: I don't know if he had the same mentality that a Kobe Bryant, that all out just was this was it.
quotes.quote: I don't know if he had the same mentality that a Kobe Bryant, that all out just was this was it. Because he was so talented. Right. Um, but again, it goes in the line of all the outstanding players Allen Iverson I played with, Steve Nash, Kobe Bryant, J-Kidd, Jamal, um, you go down the the line, Chris Webber that I played with, Alonzo Mourning in Miami. It was special. And that's when it was seven seconds or less.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Jamal Crawford's 13 points in 33 seconds
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, I was hurt that game so I was watching it from the bench.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I was hurt that game so I was watching it from the bench. It was, it was, I think we were playing San Antonio. Unbelievable. You're like, you're like, okay, we're down, it's, the next, that's, that's why I tell you, a game is not over, especially with the three ball. You get back into it, especially if the other team makes mistakes. That's why you got to stretch the game out. You got to force that other team to close the game out. If you do that, you give yourself a chance because, end of the game, some people aren't as comfortable with the ball in their hands. Some people get to the free throw line, 80% free throw shooter, can't make it when the pressure starts to dig in. And T-Mac took advantage of it.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Reggie Miller's performance against New York
quotes.excerpt: The situation played out perfectly for that person to be able to hit those shots.
quotes.quote: The situation played out perfectly for that person to be able to hit those shots because they were in tune, they were zoned in, and the moment wasn't too big. See, because if you're not mentally prepared for that moment, then it's going to miss you. You're not going to be able to step up. That's why a lot of players you'll see when they disassociate themselves with the game in late game situations, maybe it hasn't been going well, then they're not able to perform when they need to. But those that stay engaged, even if the game is not going correctly or to their liking, they're still able to make plays because they never disengaged from the game.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the Houston Rockets' underachievement
quotes.excerpt: It's so many factors. It's, you think about when Jeff Van Gundy first came in.
quotes.quote: It's so many factors. It's, you think about when Jeff Van Gundy first came in, it was Catino Mobley and Steve Francis kind of held over from Rudy Tomjanovich. It was a clash there because Jeff wanted his point guard to be disciplined in one way, a lot like Larry Brown and Allen Iverson. Right. Allen's second year, was first year was with Jimmy Lynam, let him do whatever. Here comes this disciplinarian, slow down, methodical, think, pass, get off the ball, Larry Brown. Same thing with Jeff was a little bit more relaxed with not as bad as Pat Riley, but he didn't like his point guards turning the ball over. Got to make the right play. With Rudy Tomjanovich, Steve can do whatever, isos on the wing. That was Stevie franchise. It didn't connect.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the Houston Rockets' roster changes
quotes.excerpt: So he ended up making the trade and he ended up getting Ty Lue, Ty Lue, from Orlando with Tracy.
quotes.quote: So he ended up making the trade and he ended up getting Ty Lue, Ty Lue, from Orlando with Tracy. The next year, we had a really good team, but it just didn't gel right. You know, and I end up getting traded, well, you know, waved or whatever, I traded to New Orleans and didn't go. But then injuries creeped in with Yao, injuries creeped in with T-Mac. So they never were able to get over the top and I know a lot comes down on Tracy's shoulders about not getting past the first round. And that's what happens when you're that talented. When you don't succeed in the playoffs, there are not a lot of excuses. It's, you didn't get it done.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on Tracy McGrady's reputation
quotes.excerpt: Kobe used to say Tracy was the one that gave him the most problems.
quotes.quote: Kobe used to say Tracy was the one that gave him the most problems. Yeah, Tracy 6'8, basically do a lot of stuff that Kobe could do. Right. Post, mid-post, pull-up jump shot, athletic, defensively can be a pest. Now, Kobe had the edge mentality-wise though. Yeah. That was the difference. It wasn't talent. It wasn't skill. It was the mental mentality of Kobe. That's where he made his separation. You tell me Vince Carter is not as athletically gifted as Kobe? Yeah. But they weren't as maniacal, they weren't as uber focused, they weren't diligent about as Kobe. That's not saying they they weren't diligent. We're comparing them to Kobe. In their study, their work ethic, their ability to, despite not playing well a lot of times, then matter.

quotes.quote: I have been blessed, man, to play with a lot of outstanding individuals. Allen Iverson I played with, Steve Nash, Kobe Bryant, J-Kidd, Jamal, um, you go down the the line, Chris Webber that I played with, Alonzo Mourning in Miami. It was special. But it wasn't a forced situation. It was because the ball moves so much that you're going to get open shot. And it was going from being in Houston to kind of underachieving with Yao and Tracy because of the expectations, to playing in that free flowing offense in Phoenix was just, bro, it was money.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the impact of NIL on college basketball
quotes.excerpt: It has to be controlled a little bit and I'm not talking about capping off salaries.
quotes.quote: It has to be controlled a little bit and I'm not talking about capping off salaries. Right. Why would you, you don't cap off coach's salaries, administration salaries. So why should you with players? Now, it has to be a more defined system in place, but you can't do that until you have collective bargaining. You just can't slap down and say, okay, you can do this with players. No, the labor laws don't allow that. So that's where we're going to next with NIL in college. You need a transfer portal.

quotes.speaker: Jim Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jim Jackson on the transfer portal and NIL
quotes.excerpt: I remember I seen one thing that happened, I can't remember if it was a football team.
quotes.quote: I remember I seen one thing that happened, I can't remember if it was a football team, I think they played and then the whole team just left. I think the coach, he was coaching and then the coach got a better job somewhere else. And all the players followed the coach. It happens all the time. All the players followed the coach. They all went to go play for the coach and that particular team was scheduled for a bowl game and they didn't have enough players to play. I thought that was odd, that was crazy for me. For the team to actually, but to be faced with that. Well, it's interesting because for years, coaches were had the autonomy, still do. I've seen, I'm not going to mention the coach, I've seen a coach, tournament time, NCAA, coach a team, lose, jump on the plane, go to the new university, get announced the coach later that week. Didn't fly back with the team he lost with.
